subject: Post-call: SDK & tools alignment for function-calling + reranker pilot
messages:

Subject: Post-call: SDK & tools alignment for function-calling + reranker pilot

Hi Ethan / Sara —

Thanks again for a great discovery call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum for the pilot: 

Summary of asks we captured:
- Function-calling for patient-data enrichment (demographics normalization + insurance lookup)
- Structured output for downstream ingestion (JSON schema v1 attached)
- Embeddings + light reranker for semantic patient search (targeting 2k QPS peak for search)
- Auth: customer-managed API keys + optional VPC egress for private data flows

Proposed technical approach (high-level):
1) Start a short POC using Redwood hosted API to validate tool definitions and structured output.
2) Use redirectable SDK flow for auth — SDK provides credential exchange + short-lived token.
3) Implement function-calling for enrichment with parallel tool calls for fallback (primary: internal lookup service, secondary: partner API).
4) Add embeddings + reranker on sample dataset to validate recall/latency tradeoffs.

Immediate next steps I propose (owner / due):
- Redwood: deliver SDK quickstart + sample tool definitions (Dev) — due Tue 6/13
- Pacifica: share sample CSV and golden reranker eval set (Ethan) — due Mon 6/12
- Joint: 30m tech sync to walk SDK flow and error handling (all) — propose Wed 6/14 10am PT

Attachments: pacifica-sow-draft-v1.pdf (SOW stub), redwood-sdk-quickstart.tar.gz (sample SDK + README)

If that looks good I’ll schedule the sync and loop in infra for network questions.

Thanks,
Monica

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 12 Jun 2028 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: SDK & tools alignment for function-calling + reranker pilot

Thanks Monica — adding a couple of technical clarifications to steer the POC: 

1) Tool definitions: please plan to model enrichment tools with a typed interface (inputs: patient_id, payload; outputs: status, normalized_record, error_code). That lets us validate structured output mapping without brittle text parsing.

2) Parallel tools & error handling: recommend a primary/secondary pattern with majority-configurable retry/backoff and clear error codes surfaced in the SDK. Example fallback flow: primary call -> if 5xx/timeout -> run secondary in parallel -> prefer first non-error result but keep both for reconciliation.

3) Reranker: initial approach should be a lightweight scorer that re-ranks top-K from embedding nearest neighbors rather than re-embedding on the fly. That keeps latency predictable. We should capture per-query token counts during POC to tune batching.

I’ll attach a one-page pattern doc in the follow-up; Dev, I’ll sync offline on exact schema examples so we can ship the SDK sample Monday.

- Sean

Subject: Re: Post-call: SDK & tools alignment for function-calling + reranker pilot

Ethan / Sara —

Attaching the SDK quickstart and a small set of example tool definitions. Highlights and notes: 

- SDK quickstart includes a local dev proxy that simulates short-lived tokens and shows redirect-based auth flows. See README.md in the tar for env vars.
- tool_definitions.yaml (included) uses typed schemas we can convert to JSON Schema for validation.
- Error codes: we include an explicit enum (OK, NOT_FOUND, TRANSIENT_ERROR, PERM_FAILURE) and suggest surfacing the code in the HTTP response header X-Redwood-Tool-Error.
- Parallel execution: the SDK has a helper to fanout calls with a configurable winner-selection policy (first-successful | highest-score). Default: first-successful with 2s soft window.

Notes on deployment modes:
- For POC, hosted API is fastest. If you need data-plane isolation we can switch to dedicated nodes later and preserve the same SDK config.

I’ll post the link to a short demo video by EOD.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.tar.gz

Cheers,
Dev Patel

Monica / team —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 
- We can share a 10k-row sample CSV by EOD today (patient_id, free-text notes, canonical insurance id).
- Latency target: <150ms 95th for enrichment paths if hosted; if we move to dedicated we can tolerate up to 250ms initially.
- Security: we need confirmation that token rotation meets our policy (short-lived tokens <= 12 hours) and that audit logs capture tool inputs/outputs for troubleshooting.

One operational ask: can Redwood provide a simple failure-metrics dashboard (counts by error_code) during the POC so our CS team can triage quickly?

If you can confirm the above we’ll lock in Wed 6/14 10am PT for the tech sync.

Thanks,
